thread:
anya: Hey team — I'm wiring per-model feature flags into k8s. Plan is to have a ConfigMap per model in the `models` namespace with a JSON blob the runtime will read on startup + watch for changes. Quick Q: is it okay for infra/terraform to own these ConfigMaps directly, or should we have an operator/job that syncs from S3?

anya: Proposed sample manifest (first pass):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: model-flags-bert-v2
  namespace: models
data:
  flags.json: |
    {\"enable_quant\": true, \"max_seq\": 2048, \"routing_tier\": \"gold\"}
```

anya: Also thinking terraform in infra repo will manage via `kubernetes_manifest` or `helm_release`, and any secrets referenced (like model-specific API keys) would come from ExternalSecrets (AWS KMS + SSM) not in TF state. Thoughts?

sam_k: short answer: prefer not to put frequently changing flags directly into TF-managed resources. TF state and churn = pain. If flags are relatively static (minor updates), TF is ok. If you expect many rapid updates, use a per-model admin UI + a syncer that updates ConfigMaps.

sam_k: also runtime currently expects the key to be `<model>.json` (e.g., `bert-v2.json`) rather than `flags.json`. small naming detail.

mohit: agree with sam. alternative: keep canonical config in S3 and have a small k8s Job or controller reconcile ConfigMaps from that S3 object. That avoids blowing TF state on each update. Use signed S3 objects + KMS.

lena: runtime note: loader watches `configmaps` in `models` namespace and uses filename -> model mapping. So naming matters. Also it ignores ConfigMaps above 1MB (k8s limit), so keep per-model small.

anya: great catch re: key name and size. updating example.
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: model-config-bert-v2
  namespace: models
data:
  "bert-v2.json": |
    {\"enable_quant\": true, \"max_seq\": 2048, \"routing_tier\": \"gold\"}
```

ryan: Terraform snippet if you still want infra to render the manifest (acceptable for initial rollout):
```hcl
variable "models" {
  type = map(string) # map of name -> JSON blob
}

resource "kubernetes_manifest" "model_flags" {
  for_each = var.models
  manifest = yamldecode(templatefile("${path.module}/templates/model-config.yaml.tpl", { name = each.key, payload = each.value }))
}
```

ryan: but follow sam/mohit — if these change often, put them outside TF and use a syncer. Also don't store secrets in ConfigMaps. Use ExternalSecrets or CSI driver for Secrets Store to mount credentials.

mohit: another ops note — if you plan to do canary updates to model flags (10% traffic), keep the flags in a separate key and have the router join on `routing_tier`. Canary rollout can be handled by changing the router config + target group, not the model ConfigMap itself.

ops-bot: lint: kubernetes manifest OK. Recommend enable RBAC for the syncer service account.

anya: Awesome. Plan: 1) put initial static flags for new model in infra TF for launch (low churn) 2) implement S3-backed syncer (short PoC) for rapid updates 3) move high-churn flags out of TF once syncer is stable. I'll open a PR in infra repo with the TF snippet above and the corrected file naming, and then follow up with a syncer RFC. Ping @sam_k @mohit for review. :pray:

sam_k: lgtm, please add a short doc in ops/ about the per-model config lifecycle.

mohit: +1. thanks for doing this the right way.

anya: thanks! will update PR and tag reviewers.
